title: Factory project profile (.factory/project.yaml)
description: The per-project adapter. YAML on disk, validated against this schema after parsing. See TASK-CONTRACT.md §5.

defaultRunnerConfig.description: F-46 AC-4 (M-4): test-runner configuration is judge surface — the runner decides whether the contract tests run at all — so it is protected by default, not by each profile's own list. protected_globs are whole-file globs (root AND any depth — fnmatch's **/x needs a slash before x, so the root needs its own entry) covering conftest and every dedicated pytest config name pytest discovers (pytest.ini, .pytest.ini, pytest.toml, .pytest.toml; tests/test_f46.py reads the name list from the installed pytest); they are unioned into paths.protected by the profile loader (a profile can only widen, never remove). pytest_tables names, per file, the TOML tables / configparser sections of the three SHARED config files whose content L0's diff policy compares between the merge-base and head, structurally, whatever the profile says (added or removed included; unparseable at either end, or no refs to compare, fails closed). pyproject.toml, setup.cfg and tox.ini are deliberately NOT whole-file protected: dependency bumps and tox/metadata edits must still flow to their own rules.

defaultProtectedControl.description: F-63 AC-4: the factory-control surface is protected by default, structurally — .factory/** is the security config itself (the profile, the queue), and whether it is protected must not be decided by its own content (a client-supplied or implementer-rewritten profile simply omitting the opt-in, the audit's finding). Unioned into paths.protected by the profile loader AND independently re-unioned by L0's diff policy, so a hand-built profile dict cannot narrow it either; a profile can only widen.

branch_protection.description: Declare only when GitHub answers the protection call with its plan-limit 403 (a private repo on a free plan): the factory then enforces up-to-date itself (re-validates open factory PRs against the current remote default head, F-26). Never excuses a repo that could have protection but doesn't.

concurrency.description: Open factory PRs allowed at once (default 1). A ready task waits while the limit is taken (F-26).

test.description: Runs the whole suite for the L0 gate and its min_tests floor. ONE runner invocation only (a single pytest/jest/etc. call): the floor reads the runner's single terminal result line, and a command that chains suites (pytest a && pytest b) prints several result lines, which reads as unknown — the floor is then never cleared by machine.

test_ref.description: Shell template that runs ONE named test for the L1 red-first proof. Placeholders, substituted by literal replacement (shell braces like ${VAR} pass through): {ref} = the quoted test node id, {path} and {name} = its file and test-name halves (jest-style runners take them separately), {python} = the orchestrator's interpreter. Default: python -m pytest -q {ref}.

baselines.description: Repo-relative path to a baseline file, if any

risk.description: risk flag -> list of globs. Keys must be risk flags from tasks.schema.json.

generated.description: F-65 AC-4: repo-relative globs (scope-matcher semantics) of generated files (lockfiles, snapshots, codegen output) in scope for EVERY task of this project. Owner-approved profile content (security group paths.generated under F-63); widening without re-approval refuses the run. Obeys the declared-scope refusals at load — a catch-all or climbing pattern refuses.

setup_outputs.description: Repo-relative directories the setup command creates (a venv, node_modules). L1 keeps them through its between-phase git clean, so the red and green runs have the installed tools; everything else untracked is still removed.

sentinels.description: risk flag -> project sentinels (F-25): [{command, description}]. Each command runs when the diff touches that flag's paths.risk globs; a failure FAILs the L0 verdict and escalates sentinel_failed. Keys must be risk flags from tasks.schema.json.

live_checks.description: name -> {command, secrets, when}. Run by the orchestrator OUTSIDE the agent sandbox.

secrets.description: Keychain item names exported as env vars

standards.description: Repo-relative paths of the project's coding-standards docs. Read by the L2 reviewer only, never pushed to the implementer (VALIDATOR-SPEC L2).

network_allowlist.description: Extra domains (package registries) beyond docs_allowlist and the model endpoint

sandbox.description: Sandbox capability opt-ins (factory.sandbox.build_settings). Absent means the defaults: nothing extra is granted.

allow_local_binding.description: Authorize srt's network.allowLocalBinding for the GATE RUNNER's settings only (L0/L1 commands and the stale-base re-validation clone — the project's fixed test suite, run after L0's diff policy): its tests bind sockets. The session seats (implementer, reviewer, importer) never receive it whatever this says — srt's macOS rules grant bind on ANY local address/port (not loopback-only), inbound from ANY origin, AND outbound connect to 127.0.0.1/::1 on any port (every host loopback service: a logged-in browser's DevTools ports, local databases, dev/MCP servers), reach model-written session code must not have. External-domain egress stays allowlisted. Linux: no-op (bwrap netns already allows in-namespace binds; nothing outside can reach them). Off unless a human sets it.

toolkit.description: The project's vetted agent toolkit (F-22 AC-6): names of admitted index entries (toolkit/index.yaml). Every name must be an index entry of the matching kind — an unknown name refuses the profile at load, as F-02 does for invalid state. Seats may narrow the choice (a subset), so e.g. the reviewer gets a read-only subset.

seats.description: Per-seat narrowing: each key is a seat name whose lists override (and must be a subset of) the project's own lists.
